message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Archive website

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  workflow_call:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 3 * * *"

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
    - name: Setup Python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v4
      with:
        python-version: '3.8'

    - name: Cache pip dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.cache/pip
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('.github/workflows/archive.yaml') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-pip-

    - name: Install waybackpy
      run: |
        pip install waybackpy

    - name: Archive current version of mystery-o-matic
      run: |
        waybackpy --url https://mystery-o-matic.com/ --save
",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs daily and installs the `waybackpy` package via pip on every run. Adding a pip cache step (actions/cache) avoids repeated downloads of the same dependencies, which experimental evidence shows reduces elapsed time by ~9% (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2). A job timeout of 10 minutes prevents runaway executions; simulation estimates indicate custom timeouts can reduce VM time by up to 12.9% (pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT). Explicit read-only permissions are added for least privilege. The cache key uses the workflow file hash to invalidate when the workflow changes. These changes preserve the intended archiving behavior and test coverage while reducing CI resource consumption.",
  "evidence_ids": [
    "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2",
    "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT",
    "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"
  ]
}
